cells.rationale: The latest FRED print (2026-10-02) is exactly 5.28%, and the yield has climbed about 50bp since early September; on 2026-10-05 the 10-year hit a fresh intraday 2002 high near 5.35% and Trading Economics shows it near 5.28-5.32% on 2026-10-06. With the level sitting just above the threshold and roughly five trading days to go (FOMC minutes and a 10-year auction on 2026-10-07, a 30-year auction on 2026-10-08), the outcome is close to a coin flip, tilted slightly upward by momentum and a hike-leaning Fed but tempered by the weak September payrolls (29K) that pulled yields off their highs.

Same setup as the 2026-10-13 question: the 10-year is trading around 5.28-5.32% (2026-10-06) against a 5.28% threshold after a sharp September-October selloff to 2002 highs. The September CPI release lands on 2026-10-14 itself, adding variance in both directions, so I keep this close to the baseline and slightly below the 10-13 forecast to reflect the wider spread.

note: Recorded before every entry's cutoff; scored as a separate method.
